accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS statutory framework (2024) section 1.15, characteristics of effective learning: active learning, children concentrate and keep on trying if they encounter difficulties and enjoy achievements; Development Matters (2021) on finishing and returning to activities; and the Head Start ELOF approaches to learning domain (persistence in tasks). The topic evidence (finishes a short jigsaw or drawing, says I'm finished, comes back to finish) maps one-to-one onto the jigsaw, finish routine and come-back steps. Every count in the lab and items (4 pieces, 5 and 6 blocks, 6 and 8 parts) was rechecked.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips for 3 to 4 year olds: calling a job finished when it is mostly done (jigsaw prediction 'Yes, nearly is done', the 'It's finished' tile on the face, car and house pictures), believing a pause means starting over or abandoning the job (snack-time prediction and the Knock it down choice, which empties the tower), being put off by a big job (caterpillar of 6 then 8 parts with a filling bar), and skipping the finish by announcing it before the last bit (finish routine order).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstick is about completion itself: an unfinished jigsaw whose last piece is called out, a completeness check on pictures, a paused job that survives the pause, chunked progress and a finish-say-show routine. flagtry (persisting when it is hard) works on misses as clues and keep-going thoughts, flagfocus on attention against distraction, flagbrave on trying new things; none models a job's state from started to finished. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The jigsaw only completes when the fourth piece is in and the canvas says 'One more piece!' at three; the picture step will not accept 'It's finished' until the missing eye, wheel or door is added; knocking the tower down really resets it to 0 while leaving it safe keeps 2 blocks for after snack; the bar fills one part at a time; the routine only accepts last bit, then say it, then show it. The child does each idea before the done message names it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'Yes, nearly is done' for the 3-of-4 jigsaw, 'Yes, it's finished' for the one-eyed face, and 'No, start again' for the tower after snack. The task right after each makes the child act against the wrong choice, and the done message quotes their guess through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: nearly (nearly done is not done), new (finish this one first), knock (you must start again), never (you can come back), rush (rushing makes it messy), quit (try one small bit), most (most is not all), tired (rest, then come back), bad (be proud you finished) and none (say I finished it, show a grown-up). Lab taps also name the slip, e.g. 'Not yet! It is not finished until the last bit is done.'

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short spoken sentences for a family read-aloud ('Is it done? Not yet!') and stays under the family kid limit of 5.0; the adult text stays under 10 while using the precise early-years terms: task persistence, approaches to learning, characteristics of effective learning, active learning, checking for completion, resuming, chunking and process praise.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph carries one concrete finishing idea with an example (last piece, look closely, come back after snack, one bit at a time); adult paragraphs give the framework statements, the three sub-skills, four named adult mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with the persisting, attention and trying-new-things lessons stays under 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px (iPhone 13) the 2 by 2 jigsaw frame is about 180 px wide with four 77 px tray pieces under it, the picture choices are three 74 px tall tiles across the width, the tower blocks are 70 px wide, caterpillar parts at least 24 px radius, and the young-mode buttons below the canvas are at least 56 px tall. Nothing is clipped in light or dark.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe reported no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone, no console errors, every Show me completed. Every drag or tap on the canvas has a button twin (Pick a piece and one button per space, picture choices, Add a block, Leave it safe and Knock it down, Colour the next part, one button per finishing step) and the canvas aria-label speaks each change, e.g. 'Nearly there. One more piece, then it is finished.'
